children: Shares of CarMax rose Tuesday after the used-car retailer posted better-than-expected fiscal second-quarter earnings and said it plans to resume repurchasing shares.
CarMax stock advanced 3.5% to $58.58 on Tuesday after ending Monday down 1.2%. Competitor Carvana rose 3.8%. AutoNation and Group 1 Automotive declined 3% and 2.3%, respectively.

CarMax posted adjusted earnings of $1.16 a share in the quarter ended Aug. 31, up from 64 cents a share a year ago and above Wall Street's expectation of 73 cents. Revenue grew 20% to $7.9 billion, beating the analyst consensus call for $7.09 billion, according to FactSet.

The company's gross profit per used retail vehicle came in at $2,105, down $111 from last year. Wall Street expected $2,022. CarMax said the slight decrease from a year ago reflected continued "pricing actions" to drive improved sales.
Combined retail and wholesale used vehicle unit sales increased 15% to 387,735.
Wall Street was focused unit sales and gross profit per used retail vehicle as signs of growth.
Firms on Wall Street have remained unsure on whether CarMax's business turnaround has been in gear but there has been optimism since the company's fiscal first-quarter earnings.
That optimism received a boost from the solid quarterly earnings Tuesday and there was another key detail that signaled the outlook for CarMax has changed.

The company said in a press release that it intends to resume repurchasing shares "at a modest level" in the fiscal third quarter "given our second-quarter performance, continued momentum, and improving leverage."
CarMax didn't repurchase any shares in the second quarter.
"Shifting into gear," Morgan Stanley analyst Daniela Haigian said in a research note of CarMax's earnings.
Haigian added that the stock was moving higher on the better-than-expected earnings and the company's decision to resume share repurchases.

CarMax stock as of the closing bell on Monday had advanced 8.5% since June 17, when the company reported fiscal first-quarter earnings. Shares had risen 46% this year, outperforming the S&P 500's 12% gain, as of Monday.
